1	# Getting back to the JusPrin view from classic OrcaSlicer
2	
3	Written 2026-10-27 from the code on `jusprin-newui` (ShellController.cpp, StatusRow.cpp, MainFrame.cpp/.hpp, BBLTopbar.hpp, tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp) and `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Untracked working note; not for commit.
4	
5	## The problem
6	
7	"Switch to classic view…" in the Prepare header's overflow menu (soon the gear menu, per `prepare-overflow-menu-proposal.md`) calls `detach_shell()`. That uninstalls the JusPrin shell in place: the header, panes, Home and Agent pane are destroyed, the Notebook's tab strip and the Plater sidebar come back, and stock OrcaSlicer is on screen with the same project open. The uninstall is exact and the harness checks it (`--classic-switch`).
8	
9	There is no way back in the same session. Nothing in classic view knows about JusPrin, so the only return is to quit and relaunch. Relaunch happens to work because the choice is not remembered: the `jusprin_shell` config key is read once at startup and nothing writes it. A build launched with `jusprin_shell=0` has no way into JusPrin at all.
10	
11	## The one fact that makes this cheap
12	
13	Everything a return path needs is already reachable from fork-owned code through public API, with zero new lines in OrcaSlicer-owned files:
14	
15	- `attach_shell(frame, tabpanel, main_sizer)` already receives the three things `ShellController::install` needs. `uninstall()` puts the Notebook back into that sizer, so a fresh controller's `install()` is valid again: its two preconditions (Prepare page at `tp3DEditor`, Notebook in the main sizer) hold after an uninstall. The fork only has to keep those three pointers.
16	- The macOS menu bar is `MainFrame::GetMenuBar()`. The shell already edits it by title: `show_orca_calibration_menu` removes and reinserts the Calibration menu with `FindMenu(_L("Calibration"))`.
17	- On Windows and Linux, `MainFrame::topbar()` is a public accessor the shell already uses, and `BBLTopbar::GetTopMenu()` returns the `wxMenu` behind the title-bar dropdown that holds Edit, View, Preferences and Help. Fork code can append to it.
18	- A fork-owned widget above the Notebook is just `main_sizer->Insert(...)` of a sibling, the same construction the shell uses for its own panes.
19	
20	So the design question is purely product: where the way back lives, and what survives the round trip. The rebase footprint stays at the existing six-line `MainFrame.cpp` seam.
21	
22	## Design
23	
24	### A fork-owned "classic view" controller
25	
26	New files `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ClassicView.hpp/.cpp`, one class, installed whenever the frame is in classic view: after `detach_shell()`, and at startup when `attach_shell` declines because `jusprin_shell` is `0`. Removed by the re-install. It owns two surfaces.
27	
28	**1. A banner above the Notebook (primary).** One thin row inserted into the main sizer directly above the Notebook (below the BBLTopbar on Windows and Linux), so it is on every OrcaSlicer tab: Home, Prepare, Preview, Device, Project. Left: "You're in the classic OrcaSlicer view." Right: one button, "Back to JusPrin". Not dismissible: it is the mode indicator, and the moment it is gone the way back is gone with it. Colours, height, font and the button come from the token file through `ShellTheme` and the shell recipes (design-system.md, Writing UI code); the row height can reuse the regular button height from e72f5b8070, and anything without a token gets a token and a guard first.
29	
30	**2. A View-menu row (secondary).** "Switch to JusPrin view", appended after a separator at the end of OrcaSlicer's View menu, the mirror of "Switch to classic view…". The View menu is the same `wxMenu` object on every platform: on macOS it is on the menu bar (`GetMenuBar()->GetMenu(FindMenu(_L("View")))`), on Windows and Linux it is the submenu titled View inside `topbar()->GetTopMenu()`. The lookup is by localized title, the same fragility class as the Calibration lookup. The row keeps its `wxMenuItem` id so the re-install can `Delete` it. No shortcut for now, matching the overflow-menu decision that no JusPrin shortcut list exists yet.
31	
32	The menu row exists for people who hide or ignore banners and for parity with how the person left. The banner is what makes the way back visible without knowing it exists.
33	
34	### Re-entry: `reattach_shell()`
35	
36	Fork-owned, in ShellController.cpp beside `attach_shell` and `detach_shell`:
37	
38	1. `attach_shell` records `frame`, `tabpanel` and `main_sizer` in a fork-owned static attach point the first time it runs (the MainFrame constructor). No new MainFrame accessor: `m_main_sizer` is private, and the pointer is already handed over.
39	2. `attach_shell` splits into the once-per-frame startup policy it does today (update check, the three `app_config` writes) and `install_shell()`, which builds a controller and installs it. `reattach_shell()` removes the classic-view controller, then calls `install_shell()`.
40	3. If `install_shell()` fails, the classic-view controller is put back and the person is told through OrcaSlicer's `MessageDialog` ("JusPrin's view couldn't be opened." plus the logged reason). Today's startup path only logs; at runtime a person pressed a button and must hear the answer.
41	4. The banner button and the menu row both run `frame->CallAfter(reattach_shell)`, mirroring the detach, so the handler of a widget about to be destroyed returns first.
42	5. `detach_shell()` installs the classic-view controller after `uninstall()`; `attach_shell` installs it on the `jusprin_shell == "0"` path. The shell-failed-to-install path also installs it: a retry that fails again reports through the dialog in step 3 instead of silently doing nothing.
43	
44	### What survives the round trip
45	
46	- **The project.** Model, plates, presets, undo history: OrcaSlicer owns them and the shell never touched them. Edits made in classic view are in the project when JusPrin comes back.
47	- **The project chat.** `ProjectPersistence::attach()` adopts the open project through its auxiliary data directory, so the new controller finds the same managed project document and chat. (Expected from the code path; to confirm in the harness, see below.)
48	- **Autosave.** Off in classic view: `uninstall()` drops the autosave and resumes OrcaSlicer's own backup. Classic-view edits make no JusPrin version; the first save after re-entry captures them as one version. The banner could say so in a second clause; I would leave it out unless it bites.
49	- **Not kept.** Pane widths and collapsed states reset to defaults (new controller). A model turn in flight was already cancelled by the detach. The in-memory printer or filament task chat was already lost by the detach. None of these is new.
50	
51	### Footprint and rebase risk
52	
53	- OrcaSlicer-owned files: zero new lines. Everything goes through wx public API (`GetMenuBar`, `wxSizer::Insert/Detach`), the existing public `MainFrame::topbar()` and `BBLTopbar::GetTopMenu()`, and the pointers the existing `attach_shell` call already receives.
54	- The one new dependency on upstream text is the View menu's localized title, like the existing Calibration dependency. If an upstream rename breaks the lookup, the menu row throws; `attach_shell` logs it at that boundary as it logs install failures today, and the banner, which depends on no menu, still provides the way back.
55	- The fork owns policy only (what a person in classic view can do), built on mechanisms upstream exposes. Nothing here would need to be contributed back or explained in a rebase.
56	
57	### Rejected
58	
59	- **A button in the Notebook tab strip.** `ButtonsListCtrl::GetBtnsSizer()` is public, but the strip's buttons are addressed by page position and the slice/print side buttons live there too. Zero upstream lines, but it depends on upstream internals that nothing in the strip's contract promises.
60	- **A row on OrcaSlicer's stock web homepage.** `resources/web/homepage` is upstream-owned HTML and JavaScript; a JusPrin row there is permanent, product-specific divergence.
61	- **A toggle in OrcaSlicer's Preferences dialog.** An upstream file edit, and every Preferences entry point opens JusPrin's own window while the shell is installed.
62	- **A top-level "JusPrin" menu.** Possible on macOS with zero lines, but a whole menu for one row, and Windows and Linux have no menu bar to put it on.
63	- **Restart-based return** (write `jusprin_shell=1`, ask to relaunch). Worse than the in-process path, which already exists in one direction and is tested.
64	
65	## Decisions that are Kenneth's
66	
67	1. **Banner and menu row, or menu row only.** The banner costs a row of screen on every OrcaSlicer tab for the whole classic session; it is also the only surface a person finds without knowing it is there. Menu row only keeps classic view pixel-identical to stock OrcaSlicer, and buries the way back. My pick: both.
68	2. **Remember the choice across launches.** Today classic view lasts for the session; relaunch is always JusPrin. With a return path in place it becomes safe to write `jusprin_shell` from both switches so relaunch respects the choice. My pick: keep session-only for now. JusPrin is the product and "Switch to classic view…" reads as a temporary mode; the design supports the other answer with two one-line writes if people ask.
69	3. **Wording.** Banner: "You're in the classic OrcaSlicer view." / "Back to JusPrin". Menu: "Switch to JusPrin view". Mirrors the existing row; open to change.
70

2	
3	Written 2026-10-27 from the code on `jusprin-newui` (StatusRow.cpp, LeftPaneProject.cpp, PrinterMenu.cpp, FilamentMenu.cpp, ShellController.cpp, HomeUI App.tsx) and `agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md`. Untracked working note; not for commit.
4	
5	## What the Prepare screen does
6	
7	Prepare is the project window of the new shell. One header row sits across the top:
8	
9	- Left: Home, and the toggle for the Plates and Project pane when that pane is closed.
10	- Centre: the printer-and-filament chip. Its printer half opens a menu (other printers, Printer settings…, Calibrate…, Add a printer…); its filament half opens the slot menu (filaments, colours, Use what's loaded on the printer…, Filament settings…, Calibrate this filament…).
11	- Right: the split print button (Slice / Print plate N, with Check Print, Print…, Print all plates…, Export sliced file… in its dropdown), the "…" overflow button, and the Agent-panel toggle.
12	
13	Under the header: the Plates and Project pane on the left (plate rows with Rename, Arrange, Auto-orient, Lock, Plate settings…, Delete; + Add model, + Add plate; a Project tab with the project name and save state, Details, Version history, Export project 3MF…, Print history, Edit Project Info), the 3D canvas with the tool strip (Move, Rotate, Scale, Add instance, More = OrcaSlicer's right-click menu), and the Agent pane (chat, setup card, All settings, chat navigation, Preferences › Agent for setup).
14	
15	OrcaSlicer's own menus stay on screen on every platform: the macOS menu bar (File, Edit, View, Window, Help) and, on Windows and Linux, OrcaSlicer's title bar with the same dropdowns plus Undo and Redo. The shell removes only the Calibration menu. So every OrcaSlicer command is still reachable, and the overflow menu does not need to carry them.
16	
17	## The menu today
18	
19	1. Project name with its save state ("Saved", "Saving…", "Couldn't save", "Unsaved changes"): a title row, not clickable. A warning row is added under it when autosave failed or old project data couldn't be removed.
20	2. Recent projects… (eight at a time, "Older projects…" pages on; opening one swaps the project in place)
21	3. Back to Prepare
22	4. Preferences… (⌘, / Ctrl+,)
23	5. Switch to classic view… (uninstalls the shell and shows stock OrcaSlicer)
24	
25	What is wrong with it:
26	
27	- The project name is a row you cannot click, and when the Plates and Project pane is closed it is the only place on Prepare that shows the name. The product definition says the name and save state are continuously visible, and that Project details opens "from the project name or menu". Neither holds today.
28	- "Back to Prepare" sits on the Prepare screen. It is there because Tab on the canvas still flips OrcaSlicer to its Preview tab under the JusPrin header (GLCanvas3D posts the tab event; the shell's key hook only handles Ctrl+,). Check print itself is a modal now, so the row is a repair for a leak, shown all the time.
29	- Four different scopes in one list: this project, navigation, the app, and an escape hatch.
30	
31	## Decision (Kenneth, 2026-10-27)
32	
33	The menu becomes an app-level gear menu, the same glyph as Home's Preferences button. Rows: Preferences… (⌘, / Ctrl+,) and, after a separator, Switch to classic view…. Nothing project-scoped in it.
34	
35	- Version history, Export project 3MF and Project details stay only in the Plates and Project pane's Project tab. No duplicate route from the menu: it was a discoverability hedge, not a reason.
36	- Recent projects leaves the menu. Its homes are Home's gallery and the File menu's Recent files. OrcaSlicer's File › Recent files is fed by MainFrame's file history from OrcaSlicer's own load path; whether JusPrin's managed autosave projects reach it is unverified and must be checked, and fixed if they don't.
37	- Back to Prepare goes. Tab on the canvas still flips OrcaSlicer to its Preview tab under the shell (GLCanvas3D posts the tab event; the shell's key hook only handles Ctrl+,). Stop that flip at the shell instead of keeping a repair row.
38	- Keyboard shortcuts row: skipped for now; no agreed JusPrin shortcut list exists.
39	- The project name and save state, and the two autosave warning rows ("Changes couldn't be saved. JusPrin will retry.", "Some older project data couldn't be removed."), lose their place in the menu. They need a home in the header or a failure-only status line; that is a separate header item, not part of the menu change.
40	
41	The "JusPrin v2" canvas board for the Prepare header is to be updated to this shape for review before the app changes.

44	
45	Board published on the "JusPrin v2" canvas, version 1793143597-61ea, label "Prepare header gear menu (2026-10-27)": `project/main-10-prepare-header-gear-menu` on the Main Page (light and dark header strips, the gear, a two-row popover), an orange sticky flagging the undecided home for the project name, save state and autosave warnings, and `project/prefs-13-entry-points` updated to show the gear. Only OrcaSlicer's path-keyed load paths add to the list (Plater.cpp load_project, open_3mf_file, add_file); ProjectAutosave::open_managed_project restores a checkpoint and adds nothing. Two consequences:
48	1. The list holds source-file paths, and OrcaSlicer's handler opens a path as a new project, which under the 2026-10-24 opening rules starts a new project instead of resuming the managed one.
49	2. Making File › Recent files a real home needs either a fork seam in MainFrame's recent-menu handler (map an entry to a managed project id) or a fork-owned Recent submenu fed from the same list Home uses. Feeding wxFileHistory alone is not enough. Decision pending.

51	## Recent files decision (Kenneth, 2026-10-27)
52	
53	Use OrcaSlicer's own path-keyed File › Recent files list. No fork-owned submenu, no path-to-project-id mapping. Picking an entry must behave exactly like opening that external file again from the OS: a .3mf goes through the fork seam `Plater::set_external_project_open_handler` (ShellController.cpp), which asks the "Previously opened file" question (Open existing project / Create new project / Cancel) when a saved project came from that path, and resumes the managed project on Open existing; other model files start a new project per the opening table in architecture.md. To verify in the app change: OrcaSlicer's recent-menu handler reaches `Plater::load_project` and so the seam; every JusPrin open path adds its source path to the list through OrcaSlicer's `add_to_recent_projects`.
54	
55	Light/dark: the main session is to check agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md for how light and dark are handled and draw the board accordingly.

58	
59	- Board is now one appearance mode (light, "⌘," meta, caption for Ctrl+,), version 1793145513-c889, per design-system.md "Design handoff requirements" rule 1: one canonical mode per screen, the other derives from the tokens.
60	- A Recent entry already reaches the seam: `MainFrame::open_recent_project` → `Plater::load_project(filename)` with originfile "-" → `m_external_project_open_handler` → the "Previously opened file" question. No routing change for .3mf.
61	- Missing file: OrcaSlicer's "The project is no longer available." dialog and entry removal already exist.
62	- What feeds the list: a .3mf is added by `priv::load_project` on a successful new-project load, by every JusPrin route. Model files (STL/STEP/OBJ…) are never added by any JusPrin route; OrcaSlicer adds them only from File › Import with the `recent_models` preference on (default off). OrcaSlicer's own OS open and drop of a model file do not add it either.

## Writing UI code

Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock

## Runtime application in the native app
======
### Sibling widgets and static owners must plan for destruction order

**Observed problem:** The shell's status row binds handlers on the Notebook —
a sibling, not a parent — and the shell controller lives in a static slot
that outlives `MainFrame`. wx destroys sibling children in unspecified order,
so an `Unbind` in the row's destructor could run against an already-destroyed
Notebook, and the static controller's destructor could "restore" widgets that
no longer exist.

**Resolution:** The row also binds the Notebook's `wxEVT_DESTROY` and skips
`Unbind` once the Notebook is gone. The controller binds the frame's
`wxEVT_DESTROY`, marks itself uninstalled, and abandons (rather than
restores) its canvas-presentation state, so nothing touches widgets during or
after frame teardown.

**Lesson for future agents:** An event binding on any window you do not own
needs a destruction watcher before `Unbind` is safe, and an object that
outlives the widget tree must have an abandon path that forgets pointers
without touching them. Restoring state is for runtime detach; teardown only
ever abandons.

### A canvas event posted from a command had not run when the command returned

`GLCanvas3D::post_event` queues the event with `wxPostEvent`. A workspace command
that used it to add a plate, or to tell Orca a selection changed, returned with
the plate count and the object list unchanged, and the following read saw the
old state. Commands that must have taken effect when they return raise the event
on the canvas window with `ProcessEvent` (`raise_now` in `Workspace/OrcaOutline.cpp`).

### `Plater::select_object` returns early when the canvas already holds the selection

It skips `ObjectList::update_selections()`, so the object list can still be
pointing at the plate it last showed. The object list's own commands
(`toggle_printable_state`, `set_extruder_for_selected_items`, `fix_through_cgal`)
act on the list's selection and do nothing, without an error, when it is not an
object or a copy. Bring the list up to date first, and check the effect: a
command that can silently do nothing needs its result read back.

### The object list changes the model without announcing it

Switching an object's printable state or filament through the list publishes no
project-state change, so a view built on the workspace stays as it was. The
command that calls the list publishes a Contents change itself.

### Orca gives every loaded object the first filament slot

An object's config carries `extruder = 1` from the start. It is an assignment,
not a choice, so presence of the key says nothing about whether the person chose
it; the pane shows a filament only for a multi-material job or a slot other than
the first.

### A plate carries settings only by Orca's own test

`PartPlate::config()` has keys on every plate. The plate icon's "has plate
settings" test is bed type, print sequence, first-layer and other-layers
sequences, or a spiral-mode setting; the pane uses the same one.

name: windows-ui-testing-without-a-desktop
description: How to drive real JusPrin UI gestures on the Windows box when the RDP session is disconnected (SetCursorPos and screen capture both die; send WM_ messages and read geometry instead)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: c818cfcf-07b0-4d84-a4d6-a69c1bd9fdde
  modified: 2026-10-22T01:22:43.199Z
---

When the RDP session to the Windows verification box is **disconnected** (`query session` shows state `Disc` for the `guitest` session), `SetCursorPos`/`mouse_event` silently do nothing — `GetCursorPos` keeps returning 0,0 — and `Graphics.CopyFromScreen` throws "The handle is invalid". Only a *connected* session has an input desktop.

**Why:** This looks exactly like an application bug — gestures appear to have no effect and screenshots fail — so it can burn a long time before you realise the session, not the code, is the problem.

**How to apply:**
- Check `query session` first when input or capture stops working.
- Real UI testing still works without a desktop: `SendMessageTimeout` WM_LBUTTONDOWN / WM_MOUSEMOVE / WM_LBUTTONUP / WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK straight to the child HWND. This goes through the real wxMSW window procedure, real `SetCapture`, and real double-click handling — strictly more real than the harness's `ProcessEvent` injection, which bypasses `MSWWindowProc` entirely.
- A faithful drag must hold the pointer at a fixed **screen** x and recompute the client x from the target window's live `GetWindowRect` each step. Holding client x fixed makes a moving splitter run away, because the app converts with `ClientToScreen` against the window's current position.
- Screenshots still work disconnected through `PrintWindow(hwnd, hdc, 2)` (PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT): it draws the GL canvas and WebView2 panes (confirmed 2026-10-21). CopyFromScreen may not throw but returns a blank white image. But PrintWindow often returns the GL canvas as flat grey even at rest and after RedrawWindow (2026-10-22: grey in PrintWindow, tower drawn on screen). A grey canvas in a PrintWindow capture proves nothing; with a connected session, check with CopyFromScreen before calling it a bug or calling it fine.
- Read results from `EnumChildWindows` + `GetWindowRect` rather than pixels; assert that sibling columns tile the client rect exactly, which catches overlaps a per-window size check cannot see.
- P/Invoke `GetWindowTextW` must be declared `CharSet=CharSet.Unicode`, or the StringBuilder is marshalled as ANSI and the W call overruns the buffer and crashes PowerShell.
- The harness holds `shell_integration_harness.exe` open; kill it before relinking or the link fails with LNK1104.
- See [[windows-build-machine]] for the Mesa/GL and toolchain facts.

content.text:
The way back from classic view works on Windows, but one check fails: going back opens a new, empty chat instead of the one the person had. The handoff said to stop and report if that happened, so I haven't patched it. Nothing is committed.

**What I built**
- **`Shell/ClassicView.hpp/.cpp`** (new): the banner above OrcaSlicer's tabs and the "Switch to JusPrin view" row at the end of OrcaSlicer's View menu. The banner uses `surface_canvas` as you chose, the existing label and secondary-button recipes, and a `border_subtle` bottom line. I added no tokens.
- **`ShellController.cpp/.hpp`**: `attach_shell` now remembers the window it was given. Installing the shell moved into its own function, and a new `reattach_shell()` handles the return. Classic view shows its way back in all three cases: after "Switch to classic view…", when the app starts with the shell off, and when the shell fails to install. If going back fails, OrcaSlicer's own error dialog says "JusPrin's view couldn't be opened." with the reason.
- If OrcaSlicer's View menu can't be found, only the menu row is skipped and the banner stays.
- No OrcaSlicer-owned files were edited.

**Test results (Windows harness, this machine)**
- **Two round trips:** `--classic-switch` switches to classic and back twice, first through the menu row and then through the banner button. Every presentation check passes both times: banner directly above the tabs, row present, then both gone after going back, tab strip hidden, sidebar unavailable, canvas usable. Nothing crashed or leaked over the two trips.
- **Shell-off start:** `--stock` passes 20 of 20. It starts with the shell off, the banner and row are there, and the banner opens JusPrin.
- **Guards:** `brand_tokens_tests` and `shell_theme_tests` pass.
- **Appearance:** screenshots in light and dark are attached, and both look right. The first dark capture photographed the Claude window, which was in front at the time; the second attempt worked.

**The one failure: the chat doesn't come back**
`return_keeps_the_project_chat` fails. JusPrin keeps each project's chat in its own folder, named by the project's id. When the shell comes back, it builds a new chat store and looks for the chat in the project's OrcaSlicer working folder. JusPrin never writes the chat there for these projects, so it finds nothing and starts a new project with a new id.

So after a round trip the person's earlier chat is no longer attached to the open project, though it is still on disk. The handoff assumed it would reattach. The code is `ProjectPersistence::adopt_current_project` with `ShellController::install` creating a fresh `ProjectPersistence`.

**Not verified**
- Nobody opened the Windows title-bar dropdown by hand. The harness sends the menu row's selection through the menu's own dispatch, which is the path a real click takes.
- The macOS menu-bar code compiles here but was never run.
- If someone switches dark mode inside OrcaSlicer's own Preferences while in classic view, I don't know whether the banner recolors. On Windows, OrcaSlicer doesn't send the event the banner listens for.

I also added a `--classic-switch-capture <dir>` harness flag to take the classic-view screenshot.

**Should I fix the lost chat in this change, or leave it for later?**
- **Fix it here:** when the shell comes back, reattach to the project that was open when it left, with the failing check as the test.
- **Leave it for later:** mark that check as a known failure and commit the rest.

The chat now survives a trip through classic view: going back to JusPrin over the same project reopens that project's conversation. If the person opened or started a different project while in classic view, that project gets its own new chat. Nothing is committed.

**What was wrong:** the shell coming back built a new chat store and looked for the conversation in the project's OrcaSlicer working folder. JusPrin never writes it there, so the shell found nothing and started a new project with a new id.

**The fix** (in `ShellController.cpp/.hpp`, fork-owned files only):
- When the shell switches to classic view, it now saves the open project's conversation and two markers that identify that project. One is OrcaSlicer's project session number, which changes whenever OrcaSlicer resets or replaces the project. The other is the project's working folder, which changes whenever a project is loaded or created.
- On the way back, the new shell takes up the saved conversation only if both markers still match. Otherwise it starts fresh, as it did before.
- Because the conversation keeps its old project id, autosave picks up the project's existing save history and name instead of starting a new store.
- Edits made in classic view are saved as one new version the next time the project is saved after going back.
